Now I understand. The glow issue: on pointerleave, they remove the CSS properties `--mx`/`--my` immediately (reverting to 50% 50%) while fading out the ::after highlight (opacity transition 0.3s). Result: the glow jumps to center then fades. Fix: keep the last position while fading opacity out. Best approach: add a `.is-leaving` state? Actually simplest: don't remove --mx/--my immediately; remove class is-tilting (which fades opacity) and remove properties after transition ends. Let's implement: on reset, remove class, and only remove --mx/--my after transition (e.g. 320ms). Also remove --rx/--ry immediately? Tilt should reset smoothly - currently removing --rx returns to 0deg with transition 0.55s which is fine.

But wait: the radial gradient is 360px circle at var(--mx) var(--my). When leaving, the glow should fade out in place. So keep mx/my during fade, then remove.

Note also on pointerleave, element already has is-tilting removed so transition transform 0.55s. The ::after opacity transition 0.3s.

Use a timeout stored in ref to avoid races.

Second task: background shapes should "drive away" (уезжали) and new ones appear when scrolling to certain tabs (sections). "при листании на определенные вкладки" — scrolling to certain sections. Which sections are "вкладки"? Perhaps Preview tabs? Hmm "фигуры на фоне при листании на определенные вкладки уезжали и появлялись новые" — when scrolling to certain sections, shapes should slide away and new ones appear. Likely relates to sections/nav links (header nav: Обзор, Установка, Дорожная карта...). Let's check Header.tsx to see nav items.

So sections with ids: features (Info), preview, install, roadmap, links. The user says "при листании на определенные вкладки" — when scrolling to certain sections/tabs. They want background shapes to slide away and new ones appear.

Design: a Backdrop component that tracks which section is current via IntersectionObserver (or scroll position) and transitions shape set. When the active scene changes, old shapes translate off (e.g. up/down or left/right) and fade, new ones enter.

Implementation approach: keep a scene index; render shapes per scene with a `key={scene}` wrapper, CSS animation for enter, and on old scene exit animation. Simpler and robust: on scene change, render two layers: outgoing layer with `.is-leaving` class animating translate, incoming with animate in. Need to retain outgoing shapes to animate out then unmount after 700ms.

Simpler still: reuse same 6 shape elements but assign new positions per scene, and on change add a "wave" class that drives them off then new ones in? But user explicitly wants old shapes to leave and new ones appear. Use two layers with transitions.

Let me design Backdrop:

```tsx
const SCENES: Shape[][] = [...] // per-section shape sets
const SECTION_IDS = ['hero','features','preview','install','roadmap','links'] ;
```

Backdrop observes elements with ids. Use scroll-based: determine current scene = last section whose top is above mid viewport. Simpler: IntersectionObserver on sections with rootMargin '-45% 0px -45% 0px' threshold 0 → count intersection; pick topmost intersecting. Hero has no id... Home hero section? # In-app browser

The browser tools drive a Chromium browser inside the user's OpenCode desktop app. Its tabs show in the app's Review pane, so the user sees what you do and can use the same tabs. Call the tools from code mode as `tools.browser.*`; `search({ namespace: "browser" })` lists their exact signatures.

await tools.browser.wait({ tabID: tab.id, condition: "load" })
const errors = await tools.browser.console({ tabID: tab.id, level: "error" })
